implementation.explanation: Only YoutubeSetupActivity.kt changes. On API 33 and later, onCreate registers a platform OnBackInvokedCallback at PRIORITY_DEFAULT through onBackInvokedDispatcher, after setContentView. onDestroy unregisters it. The callback is stored as Any? and only cast inside @TargetApi(33) helpers behind SDK_INT checks, so older devices never resolve android.window classes. No dependency, manifest opt-out or theme change is added. The legacy onBackPressed override stays as the fallback for devices below API 33 and for API 33 to 35 without the manifest opt-in, where the platform ignores dispatcher callbacks. Android dispatches each Back event to only one of these paths. System Back, the legacy fallback and the header arrow now all call navigateBack(). A sub-page shows OVERVIEW through the existing show()/rerender path, which keeps the saved route and expanded state. On the overview it calls finish() explicitly, returning to the originating Patcher screen. The old super.onBackPressed() is removed and nothing re-dispatches Back, so there is no recursion. Authentication, patchPending and request-code rotation, source and picker locks, result handling, signing, keyboard settings and all NexusUi kit views are untouched. This is a behavioural fix, so the frontend-design skill was applied as restraint: no visual change, consistent with the round-4 kit approval. I did not execute builds, tests, emulator or device checks. The parent should still verify the following on the installed phone with KEYCODE_BACK and the header arrow: Nexus → Patcher → Set up YouTube → MicroG → Back reaches the YouTube overview, and a second Back returns to Patcher. The same check is still needed on a pre-33 or non-opted-in API 33 to 35 path, and Fable approval is required before building.
